title: SpO₂, Temperature and Capillary Refill — Reading the Small Numbers Safely

hook.en: A clip on the finger, a probe in the ear and a press on the nail bed can warn you about low oxygen, infection and poor circulation. Learn the correct technique and the traps that make these numbers lie.
hook.ur: Ungli par clip, kaan mein probe aur nail bed par dabao kam oxygen, infection aur kharab circulation se khabardar kar sakte hain. Sahi technique aur woh jaal seekhein jin se yeh numbers jhoot bolte hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll use a pulse oximeter, a thermometer and capillary refill correctly, know the normal values and the stop rules for exercise.
goal.ur: End tak aap pulse oximeter, thermometer aur capillary refill sahi use karenge, normal values aur exercise ke stop rules jaanenge.

text.en: **SpO₂** (oxygen saturation) shows the percentage of haemoglobin carrying oxygen: **95–100%** is normal; below **92%** tell the nurse or doctor; stop exercise below **88–90%** (or lower targets in chronic lung disease, as prescribed). **Temperature** normal is about **36.1–37.2 °C**; fever starts from 38 °C and below 35 °C is hypothermia. **Capillary refill time** (press a nail bed for 5 seconds, release) should be **under 2 seconds**.
text.ur: **SpO₂** (oxygen saturation) batata hai ke haemoglobin ka kitna percent oxygen utha raha hai: **95–100 %** normal; **92 %** se neeche nurse ya doctor ko batayein; **88–90 %** se neeche exercise rok dein (ya chronic lung disease mein kam targets, jaise prescribe hon). **Temperature** normal takriban **36.1–37.2 °C**; bukhar 38 °C se shuru aur 35 °C se neeche hypothermia hai. **Capillary refill time** (nail bed ko 5 seconds dabayein, chhor dein) **2 seconds se kam** honi chahiye.

text.en: A pulse oximeter is a torch shining through your finger. Oxygen-rich blood and oxygen-poor blood absorb red light differently, so the device compares the two colours of light that come out the other side. Anything that blocks the light (nail varnish, cold fingers, movement) confuses it.
text.ur: Pulse oximeter ungli ke aar paar roshni dalne wali torch hai. Oxygen se bhara khoon aur oxygen ki kami wala khoon laal roshni ko mukhtalif tareeqay se jazb karte hain, is liye device doosri taraf nikalne wali do rangon ki roshni ko compare karta hai. Jo cheez roshni rokay (nail varnish, thandi ungliyan, harkat) usay confuse kar deti hai.

intro.en: Warm the hands and remove nail varnish. Clip the probe on a finger so the light shines through the nail bed and keep the hand still. **Wait for a steady waveform and a stable number** before you read it: a poor waveform means a poor reading.
intro.ur: Haath garam karein aur nail varnish utaar dein. Probe ko ungli par aise clip karein ke roshni nail bed se guzre aur haath ko saakin rakhein. **Steady waveform aur stable number ka intezar** karein phir parhein: kharab waveform ka matlab kharab reading.

question.en: A patient's SpO₂ reads 82%, but the waveform is jagged, the hand is cold and the patient is shivering. What should you do first?
question.ur: Patient ka SpO₂ 82 % hai lekin waveform ragged hai, haath thanda hai aur patient kaanp raha hai. Pehle kya karein?

text.en: Warm the hand, keep it still, try another finger and check the patient clinically before acting on the number
text.ur: Haath garam karein, saakin rakhein, doosri ungli try karein aur number par amal se pehle patient ko clinically dekhein

feedback.en: Yes — poor perfusion, cold and movement give false lows; look at the patient and repeat.
feedback.ur: Haan — kharab perfusion, thand aur harkat jhooti kam reading deti hain; patient ko dekhein aur dohrayein.

text.ur: Bina check kiye foran oxygen shuru karein

feedback.en: Check the patient and the reading first; a true low reading with symptoms still needs a nurse or doctor.
feedback.ur: Pehle patient aur reading check karein; sachchi kam reading symptoms ke saath bhi nurse ya doctor ko chahiye.

text.en: Ignore the reading since it is always wrong
text.ur: Reading nazar-andaz karein kyunke hamesha ghalat hoti hai

feedback.en: It is often right; the point is to confirm.
feedback.ur: Yeh aksar sahi hoti hai; maqsad tasdeeq hai.

intro.en: Clean the probe, pull the ear gently **up and back** to straighten the ear canal and place the probe snugly. Wait for the beep, then read and record the value **and the route** (ear, forehead, mouth or armpit). Normal about 36.1–37.2 °C; fever from 38 °C; below 35 °C is hypothermia.
intro.ur: Probe saaf karein, kaan ko aahista **upar aur peechay** kheench kar ear canal seedhi karein aur probe ko achi tarah rakhein. Beep ka intezar karein, phir value **aur route** (kaan, maatha, munh ya bagal) parh kar likhein. Normal takriban 36.1–37.2 °C; bukhar 38 °C se; 35 °C se neeche hypothermia.

intro.en: With the hand at heart level in a warm room, press the nail bed (or the sternum) for 5 seconds until it blanches, release and count how long the pink colour takes to return. **Under 2 seconds is normal**; longer suggests poor perfusion, cold, shock or dehydration.
intro.ur: Haath dil ki level par, garam kamre mein, nail bed (ya sternum) ko 5 seconds dabayein jab tak safed na ho, chhor dein aur ginein ke gulabi rang wapas aane mein kitni der lagti hai. **2 seconds se kam normal** hai; zyada waqt kharab perfusion, thand, shock ya dehydration batata hai.

title.en: Three quick checks, three stop rules
title.ur: Teen tez checks, teen stop rules

rows.en: Below 92 %: tell the nurse or doctor; stop exercise below 88–90 % (or the prescribed target)
rows.ur: 92 % se neeche: nurse ya doctor ko batayein; 88–90 % (ya prescribed target) se neeche exercise rok dein

rows.en: Fever from 38 °C (do not exercise a febrile patient); below 35 °C is hypothermia
rows.ur: Bukhar 38 °C se (bukhar wale patient ko exercise na karwayein); 35 °C se neeche hypothermia

rows.en: Longer suggests poor perfusion, shock, cold or dehydration: check pulse and BP and escalate
rows.ur: Zyada waqt kharab perfusion, shock, thand ya dehydration batata hai: pulse aur BP check karein aur escalate karein

text.en: **Believing the number over the patient.** An oximeter can read normally in carbon monoxide poisoning, falsely low in cold or moving hands, and less accurately in **darker skin tones** (it can over-estimate oxygen). A forehead thermometer may read lower than a core temperature. Capillary refill is slower in a cold room or in older adults. Always look at the patient (colour, breathing, alertness) and recheck an odd reading before acting.
text.ur: **Number par bharosa, mareez par nahi.** Carbon monoxide poisoning mein oximeter normal parh sakta hai, thandi ya hilti hui ungliyon mein jhooti kam, aur **gehri jild** mein kam durust (oxygen ko zyada dikha sakta hai). Maathe ka thermometer core temperature se kam parh sakta hai. Capillary refill thande kamre ya buzurgon mein sust hoti hai. Hamesha patient ko dekhein (rang, saans, hoshyari) aur ajeeb reading par amal se pehle dobara check karein.

question.ur: Kaun si finding ka matlab hai “abhi exercise rok dein”?

text.en: SpO₂ falling below about 88–90 % with breathlessness or dizziness
text.ur: SpO₂ takriban 88–90 % se neeche girna saans phoolne ya chakkar ke saath

feedback.en: Yes — symptoms plus a falling saturation mean the patient is not tolerating the load.
feedback.ur: Haan — symptoms aur girti saturation ka matlab hai patient bojh bardasht nahi kar raha.

text.en: **Use them as a bundle.** A patient with new breathlessness, a respiratory rate of 26, SpO₂ of 90%, a temperature of 38.4 °C and a refill of 3 seconds is telling a story of possible infection or sepsis: do not exercise; escalate with the numbers (use NEWS2 if your ward does). Record the values with the activity and oxygen status ("SpO₂ 94% on air at rest, 91% after 2 minutes walking") so changes are comparable.
text.ur: **Inhein ek saath use karein.** Naya saans phoolna, respiratory rate 26, SpO₂ 90 %, temperature 38.4 °C aur refill 3 seconds wala patient mumkina infection ya sepsis ki kahani sunata hai: exercise na karwayein; numbers ke saath escalate karein (agar ward use karta ho to NEWS2). Values ko activity aur oxygen status ke saath likhein (“SpO₂ aaraam mein hawa par 94 %, 2 minute chalne ke baad 91 %”) taake tabdeeliyan compare ho saken.

question.en: Why must you record the thermometer route (ear, forehead, mouth, armpit)?
question.ur: Thermometer ka route (kaan, maatha, munh, bagal) likhna kyun zaroori hai?

answer.en: Because different sites give different readings (axillary is usually lower than oral, tympanic depends on technique), and trends are only meaningful when compared like with like. A "37.1" taken in the armpit is not the same as a "37.1" in the ear.
answer.ur: Kyunke mukhtalif jagahein mukhtalif readings deti hain (bagal aam taur par munh se kam, tympanic technique par depend), aur trends tabhi mayne rakhte hain jab ek jaise ki ek jaise se muqabla ho. Bagal se li gayi “37.1” kaan wali “37.1” ke barabar nahi.

question.en: A patient with COPD has a target SpO₂ of 88–92%. Their reading is 90%. What does this mean?
question.ur: COPD ke patient ka target SpO₂ 88–92 % hai. Un ki reading 90 % hai. Iska kya matlab hai?

text.en: It is within their prescribed target, so no automatic alarm, but watch symptoms
text.ur: Yeh un ke prescribed target ke andar hai, is liye khud-ba-khud alarm nahi, lekin symptoms par nazar rakhein

feedback.en: Yes — targets are individualised; high oxygen can be harmful in some COPD patients.
feedback.ur: Haan — targets individual hote hain; kuch COPD patients mein zyada oxygen nuksan deh ho sakti hai.

text.en: It is dangerously low in everyone
text.ur: Yeh sab ke liye khatarnak taur par kam hai

feedback.en: For this patient it is the intended range.
feedback.ur: Is mareez ke liye yeh matloob range hai.

text.en: It means the oximeter is broken

feedback.en: It is a plausible, intended value.

text.en: **Call for help** for SpO₂ below 90% at rest with distress, a temperature above 38.5 °C with confusion, stiff neck or rash, a temperature below 35 °C, or a capillary refill longer than 3 seconds with a fast pulse and low blood pressure (shock). Do not exercise a patient who is febrile or acutely unwell.
text.ur: **Madad bulayein** agar SpO₂ aaraam mein 90 % se kam aur takleef ho, temperature 38.5 °C se upar confusion, gardan ki sakhti ya rash ke saath ho, temperature 35 °C se neeche ho, ya capillary refill 3 seconds se zyada, tez pulse aur kam blood pressure ke saath ho (shock). Bukhar wale ya acutely bimar patient ko exercise na karwayein.

summary.en: SpO₂ 95–100 % is normal; tell a nurse below 92 % and stop exercise below about 88–90 % (or the prescribed target).
summary.ur: SpO₂ 95–100 % normal; 92 % se neeche nurse ko batayein aur takriban 88–90 % (ya prescribed target) se neeche exercise rok dein.

summary.en: Temperature 36.1–37.2 °C (fever from 38 °C), always record the route; capillary refill should be under 2 seconds.
summary.ur: Temperature 36.1–37.2 °C (bukhar 38 °C se), hamesha route likhein; capillary refill 2 seconds se kam honi chahiye.

summary.en: Never trust a number over the patient: warm hands, remove nail varnish, wait for a steady waveform and recheck odd readings.
summary.ur: Number ko mareez se zyada na maanein: haath garam karein, nail varnish utarein, steady waveform ka intezar karein aur ajeeb readings dobara check karein.

front.en: When do you stop exercise based on SpO₂?
front.ur: SpO₂ ki bunyad par exercise kab rokte hain?

back.en: Below about 88–90 % (or the prescribed target), especially with symptoms.
back.ur: Takriban 88–90 % (ya prescribed target) se neeche, khaas taur par symptoms ke saath.

back.en: Under 2 seconds after pressing the nail bed for 5 seconds.
back.ur: Nail bed ko 5 seconds dabane ke baad 2 seconds se kam.

front.en: Normal body temperature range and fever threshold?
front.ur: Jism ke temperature ki normal range aur bukhar ki hadd?

back.ur: Takriban 36.1–37.2 °C; bukhar 38 °C se; 35 °C se neeche hypothermia.

front.en: Two things that give a falsely low oximeter reading?
front.ur: Oximeter ki jhooti kam reading ki do wajahein?

back.en: Cold hands or poor perfusion, and movement (also nail varnish).
back.ur: Thande haath ya kharab perfusion, aur harkat (nail varnish bhi).
